en.title: Mortgage of Land Explained Simply
en.directAnswer: A mortgage uses an interest in specific immovable property as security for a debt or other covered obligation. The exact legal effect depends on the type of mortgage and the documents used. A buyer should check whether land is already mortgaged before purchase.

atAGlance.whoFor: A borrower or buyer wants to understand a property mortgage.
atAGlance.mainRule: A mortgage uses an interest in specific immovable property as security for a debt or other covered obligation. The exact
atAGlance.updateStatus: Re-check the Ministry mortgage-search feature and any updated lender/registration process before publication.

en.lawMeaning:
Do not say that a lender automatically “owns” mortgaged land. The legal rights depend on the mortgage form and current documents.

This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Obtain release/redemption documents when debt is cleared.
Buyers should check available mortgage records.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A buyer finds a seller’s property in a mortgage search. The buyer should not assume the debt is cleared because the seller says so. Ask for lender evidence and proper release.
commonMistakes: Buying mortgaged land without lender clearance.
assuming title deed possession alone explains the legal position..
en.specialistTrigger: Foreclosure/default; disputed loan; missing original deeds; multiple lenders; sale of mortgaged property.
